sentences.text: Revenue compounded 6.4% a year from $38.5 billion in FY2016 to $67.6 billion in FY2025 [F1][F10][F201].
The path was cyclical: revenue fell 22.4% in FY2020 and rose 22.1% in FY2021 [D198][D251].
The FY2020 fall came from lower sales volume on weaker end-user demand and dealer inventory cuts [P59][D198].
Operating income compounded 28.6% a year to $11.2 billion, from a FY2016 base depressed by a $595 million Resource Industries goodwill impairment [F20][F202][X111][P66].
Power & Energy sales rose 11.6% to $32.2 billion in FY2025, adding 5.2pp of growth, with Power Generation up 32.5% [D758][S102][D759][D894]; the filings cited do not say why.
Construction Industries fell 1.6%, subtracting 0.6pp from growth [D765][D766].
Its decline reflected $1.136 billion of unfavorable price realization, partly offset by $568 million of higher volume [P8][D765].
Operating costs outgrew revenue by 4.8pp, and the incremental operating margin was -69.1% [D489][D488].
Diluted shares fell 3.5%, so EPS fell 14.7% against a 17.7% drop in net income [D483][D467][D465].
Operating margin of 16.5% is above the 14.3% window median, below the 20.2% high and above the 3.0% low [F30][D1123][D1122][D1121].
It fell 3.7pp in FY2025, with cost of revenue costing 4.2pp while R&D and SG&A were roughly neutral [D476][D490][D491][D492].
Management cites $2.148 billion of unfavorable manufacturing costs, largely higher tariffs, and $817 million of unfavorable price realization [P9][D490].
The largest rise was FY2023, up 6.0pp, with cost of revenue adding 5.8pp on price, volume and the absence of a $925 million Rail goodwill impairment [D370][D384][P31][X117].
Net margin of 13.1% fell 3.5pp as the effective tax rate rose to 24.0% from 19.7% [F50][D477][D449][D396].
Operating cash flow was 1.32x net income and free cash flow 1.00x, against a 0.96x window median [D450][D451][D1135].
Free cash flow margin was 13.2%, above the 11.9% median [D447][D1129].
Capex rose 41.9% to 4.2% of revenue and 1.25x D&A, against 0.37x in FY2016 [D470][D446][D452][D10]; the filings cited do not explain the step-up.
In Machinery, Power & Energy, operating cash flow rose to $12.278 billion from $11.437 billion on lower working capital requirements and lower cash taxes [P4].
Net debt was $26.2 billion against $24.9 billion a year earlier, after total debt rose 14.1% [D456][D403][D485].
Net cash of -38.8% of revenue ranks at the 43rd percentile among seven industrials peers, whose median is -35.6% [D457][D1151][D1152].
Return on average equity of 43.5% ranks at the 100th percentile among six peers, whose median is 23.3% [D462][D1155][D1156].
Buybacks of $5.19 billion and dividends of $2.75 billion took 89.0% of free cash flow [X140][X150][D459].
Diluted shares fell 3.5%, while acquisitions were only $47 million [D483][X160].
Tariff costs drove operating income down 14.7%, and the first-quarter 2026 outlook still cites incremental tariff costs [D464][P9][P14].
It matters because the cost hit outweighed volume gains, leaving the incremental margin negative [D488].
Net debt rose for a second year, to $26.2 billion from $22.1 billion in FY2023 [D456][D350][R1].
With payouts at 89.0% of free cash flow, further buybacks would likely be debt-funded [D459][D456].
The FY2024 revenue decline of 3.4% to $64.8 billion came from lower equipment volume and reversed with 4.3% growth in FY2025, so I treat it as benign [F9][D410][R2][P22][D463].
Net income for FY2021 to FY2025 in the table is proxy-sourced; the FY2025 10-K figure of $8.88 billion differs by under 0.1% and changes no conclusion [X20][R3].
Operating margin holding above the 14.3% median would confirm resilience; a fall below it would reverse the view (FY2026 10-K) [D1123].

Construction Industries price realization turning favorable, after $1.136 billion unfavorable in FY2025 and guidance for favorable price in the first quarter of 2026, would confirm recovery (FY2026 10-K) [P8][P15].
Free cash flow to net income staying above the 0.96x median while capex exceeds 1.25x D&A would show conversion holding (FY2026 10-K) [D1135][D452].
Net debt narrowing below $24.9 billion would reverse the leverage trend; staying above $26.2 billion would extend it (FY2026 10-K) [D403][D456].
